{{Short description|Number that has fewer digits than the number of digits in its prime factorization}}
In [[number theory]], an '''extravagant number''' (also known as a '''wasteful number''') is a [[natural number]] in a given [[radix|number base]] that has fewer digits than the number of digits in its [[prime factorization]] in the given number base (including [[exponentiation|exponents]]).<ref name="Darling102">{{cite book |title=The universal book of mathematics: from Abracadabra to Zeno's paradoxes |last=Darling |first=David J. |year=2004 |publisher=[[John Wiley & Sons]] |isbn=978-0-471-27047-8 |page=102 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nnpChqstvg0C&pg=PA102 }}</ref> For example, in [[base 10]], 4&nbsp;=&nbsp;2<sup>2</sup>, 6&nbsp;=&nbsp;2×3, 8&nbsp;=&nbsp;2<sup>3</sup>, and 9&nbsp;=&nbsp;3<sup>2</sup> are extravagant numbers {{OEIS|id=A046760}}.

There are infinitely many extravagant numbers in every base.<ref name="Darling102" />

==Mathematical definition==
Let <math>b > 1</math> be a number base, and let <math>K_b(n) = \lfloor \log_{b}{n} \rfloor + 1</math> be the number of digits in a natural number <math>n</math> for base <math>b</math>. A natural number <math>n</math> has the prime factorisation
: <math>n = \prod_{\stackrel{p \,\mid\, n}{p\text{ prime}}} p^{v_p(n)}</math>
where <math>v_p(n)</math> is the [[p-adic valuation|''p''-adic valuation]] of <math>n</math>, and <math>n</math> is an '''extravagant number''' in base <math>b</math> if
: <math>K_b(n) < \sum_{{\stackrel{p \,\mid\, n}{p\text{ prime}}}} K_b(p) + \sum_{{\stackrel{p^2 \,\mid\, n}{p\text{ prime}}}} K_b(v_p(n)).</math>
